title: Zeeman spin quantum geometry and intrinsic gyrotropic spin current
abstract: We uncover an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) driven solely by an oscillating magnetic field, arising from the spin version of Zeeman quantum geometry. Using the density matrix formalism, we derive the IGSC in the low-frequency clean limit, in terms of the Zeeman spin quantum metric and the Zeeman spin Berry curvature. The effect is studied in a minimal Rashba-Dresselhaus model that also supports intrinsic gyrotropic charge currents from the Zeeman Berry curvature. The spin and charge currents exhibit a $π/2$ phase shift and are found to be perpendicular to each other for certain parameter ranges. This not only enables spin current detection but also opens pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics. We further observe that these currents switch directions between longitudinal and transverse relative to the applied field, depending on the relative strength of Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions.
summary: This work theoretically derives an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) in a 2DEG system subjected to an oscillating magnetic field. By utilizing the Zeeman spin quantum geometry, the authors show that the current has both in-phase and $\pi/2$-out-of-phase components. This mechanism offers a pathway to generate pure spin currents, which is highly relevant for developing energy-efficient spintronic devices.
main_problem: The paper uncovers an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) driven solely by an oscillating magnetic field, originating from the spin version of Zeeman quantum geometry.
main_result: The IGSC exhibits distinct in-phase (conduction) and $\pi/2$-out-of-phase (displacement) responses, enabling pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics.
method: The analysis uses the density matrix formalism, deriving the current using the Zeeman spin quantum metric and the Zeeman spin Berry curvature in the low-frequency clean limit.
model_or_system: The study is performed on a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) modeled by a Rashba-Dresselhaus Hamiltonian, incorporating Zeeman coupling from an oscillating magnetic field.
key_observables: Intrinsic Gyrotropic Spin Current (IGSC), Zeeman Spin Quantum Metric (ZSQM), and Zeeman Spin Berry Curvature (ZSBC).
important_parameters: Oscillating magnetic field frequency ($\omega$), Rashba ($\alpha$) and Dresselhaus ($ eta$) SOC strengths, and the relative strength of $\alpha$ vs. $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The calculation is performed in the low-frequency clean limit, and approximations are made regarding the expansion of the current calculation around $\eta=0$.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows the $k$-space distribution of IGSC components for pure Rashba, pure Dresselhaus, and mixed cases. Figure 3 plots the IGSC amplitude dependence on the chemical potential ($\mu$).
paper_structure: The paper derives the IGSC using the density matrix formalism, analyzes the contributions from ZSQM and ZSBC, and then investigates the resulting spin and charge current components in different regimes ($\mu>0$ vs. $\mu<0$) and SOC parameter ratios ($\alpha$ vs. $ eta$).
why_interesting: The explicit connection between geometric concepts (Berry curvature, quantum metric) and measurable transport phenomena (spin/charge currents) provides a powerful theoretical framework applicable to spintronics and topological materials.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly derives an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) in a 2DEG system using concepts like Zeeman spin Berry curvature, which is a highly relevant theoretical mechanism for energy-efficient spintronics.
